A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the re allocation effect of asymmetric partial ownership is a positive effect for consumer surplus, but it is a mixed effect for producer and total surplus.
the presence of passive ownership can increase the welfare of the society, but the effect depends on the type of ownership and the type of innovation.
PPOs are not necessarily harmful to welfare.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the re allocation effect is not a mere by product of asymmetric PPOs but is a fundamental driver of market outcomes.
, when the market is characterized by quality enhancing innovation, the presence of silent financial interests can be welfare enhancing.
